conditions-mineurs.html: ← Back to the CAPSOA home page

Registration for the CAPSOA app is reserved for people aged 15 or over. When registering, you must provide your correct date of birth. If the declared date indicates that you are under 15, registration is refused.

Users aged 15 to 17 have restricted access, as described in these conditions. Creating and sending CAPS and making payments are reserved for people aged 18 or over.

To open the content of a received CAPS, two conditions must be met: you must have turned 18 and the CAPS’ scheduled opening date must have been reached.

If you are aged 15 to 17, you can create a restricted-access account to accept or decline a CAPS intended for you and find your pending CAPS in “My CAPS”.

You can also access “My Account”, contact support and view the “Discover CAPSOA” pages and the app’s legal documents.

Your date of birth cannot be changed directly in the app. If you made a mistake when registering, you can ask support to correct it at contact@capsoa.fr. Checks may be necessary before any correction.

Before turning 18, you cannot create or send CAPS, make payments or view photos or videos in received CAPS. Accepting a CAPS does not allow you to open its content early.

The restricted access offered to users aged 15 to 17 is free. Accepting a CAPS does not entail any subscription, purchase or obligation to pay later for its recipient.

If you are a minor, we encourage you to tell your legal representative about your registration and review CAPSOA’s terms of use and privacy policy with them.

A person with parental responsibility may contact support at contact@capsoa.fr to ask a question or request deletion of their child’s account to protect the child’s interests. Each request is examined after the necessary checks on the requester’s identity and capacity as legal representative.

Using CAPSOA to send a minor content that is illegal, sexual, threatening, harassing or likely to harm their safety or dignity is prohibited.

Users aged 15 to 17 cannot view photos or videos in received CAPS. Opening them requires having turned 18 and reached the CAPS’ scheduled opening date.

If you accept a CAPS whose scheduled opening date falls before your eighteenth birthday, its opening is automatically postponed until you turn 18. The CAPS remains stored pending that opening, at no additional cost to you.

If the scheduled opening date falls after your eighteenth birthday, that date remains unchanged.

Any user or legal representative can report a CAPS, a sender or concerning behaviour to support at contact@capsoa.fr, even if the CAPS’ content has not been opened.

CAPSOA examines reports and takes measures appropriate to the situation. These may include restricting access or suspending an account.

CAPSOA uses your personal data to manage your restricted-access account and the CAPS intended for you.

Your date of birth is used to check that you meet the minimum registration age, determine which features you can access and, if necessary, postpone the opening of your CAPS until you turn 18.

The privacy policy explains which data is used, why, with which providers it may be shared, how long it is kept and what your rights are.

For any question or request about your personal data, you or your legal representative can contact support at contact@capsoa.fr.

If you are aged 15 to 17, you can access the home page, “My Account”, “My CAPS”, the “Discover CAPSOA” pages, the legal documents and support contact details. You can accept or decline CAPS intended for you and view their pending status.

You cannot create or send CAPS, make payments or view photos or videos in received CAPS.

Accepting a CAPS before turning 18 does not allow you to view its content early. Its opening remains subject to the age and date conditions in Article 4, including postponement until your eighteenth birthday when the original scheduled date is earlier.
7 - Responsibility and compliance with age restrictions

You must provide your correct date of birth and comply with the restrictions applicable to your age. Providing false information or bypassing measures restricting access to features and content is prohibited.

Where a false declaration or circumvention is identified, CAPSOA may restrict or suspend account access while examining the situation and request only the supporting documents strictly necessary for that verification.

A false declaration on your part does not release CAPSOA from its own obligations. CAPSOA remains liable for breaches of its legal or contractual obligations as provided by law.

These conditions may be updated to reflect changes to CAPSOA, measures protecting minors or applicable regulations.

The update date appears on this page. In the event of a significant change, you will be informed in the app or by email, in clear terms suited to your age.

Where a change requires your renewed acceptance or permission from your legal representative, this will be requested before the change applies to your situation.
politique-confidentialite.html: Privacy policy — CAPSOA

PRIVACY POLICY
Last updated: 24 October 2026
1 - Data collected
When creating your CAPSOA account, the following information is mandatory:
Your surname and first name, which you may change once only.
Your email address, which must be verified.
Your telephone number, which must also be verified.
Your date of birth, which cannot be changed from your account.
Your sex, used to offer the corresponding descriptions when you choose how to be identified by a CAPS recipient. This information cannot be changed from your account.
Registration cannot be completed without the mandatory information and required verifications. Country is optional. Your postal address is not requested.
You sign in using your email address and a password.
When you create a CAPS, CAPSOA collects the photos and videos you add, and the identity or description you choose to present yourself to the recipient.
When you specify a recipient who does not have a CAPSOA account, you provide their telephone number and/or email address so that their invitation can be sent.
If information that you can no longer change from your account is incorrect, you can request its correction at contact@capsoa.fr. Appropriate verification may be necessary before any correction.
2 - Use of data
CAPSOA uses your personal data to operate your account and enable CAPS to be created, sent, received and opened.

Your email address is your sign-in identifier. Your email address and telephone number also enable communications necessary to operate the service, including invitations and reminders concerning your CAPS.

Your surname and first name allow your identity to be offered among the display options when creating a CAPS. Your sex determines the descriptions offered when choosing how to be identified by the recipient.

Your date of birth determines your declared age and enables registration conditions and restrictions for minors to be applied. In particular, it allows the opening of a CAPS to be postponed until your eighteenth birthday where necessary.
If you provide your country, this information is used for indicative purposes to understand users’ geographical origins.
Photos and videos added to your CAPS are used to preserve their content and make it accessible to their recipients under the applicable opening conditions and dates.
Recipient contact details provided by the sender enable an invitation and related reminders to be sent, even if the recipient does not yet have a CAPSOA account.
3 - Recipients and sharing of data
Personal data is accessible to people authorised to manage CAPSOA, within the scope of their duties and the needs of the service.
CAPSOA also uses the following services:
Google Firebase and Google Cloud for authentication, hosting, storage of data and content, and push notifications.
Brevo, for emails and SMS related to the service.

Apple and Google, for processing in-app purchases made on iPhone and Android respectively. CAPSOA receives the transaction information needed to validate and track purchases, without receiving your bank card details.
Your CAPS recipients can access the presentation information you choose to share with them and, when the opening conditions are met, the content intended for them.
Providers receive the data necessary for the services they deliver. Depending on their role, they process it on behalf of CAPSOA or under their own obligations and privacy policies.
Data may also be disclosed to competent authorities when required by a legal obligation.
4 - Data security
CAPSOA implements appropriate technical and organisational measures to protect personal data against loss, alteration, disclosure or unauthorised access.
These measures include user authentication and access controls designed to limit viewing and modification of data to authorised persons, according to their role and the conditions for accessing CAPS.
You must keep your password and the verification codes you receive confidential. If you suspect unauthorised use of your account, contact contact@capsoa.fr.
No IT system can guarantee absolute security. This limitation does not reduce CAPSOA’s data protection obligations.
In the event of a personal data breach, CAPSOA takes the necessary measures to limit its consequences and, where required by regulation, notifies the CNIL and informs the people concerned.
5 - Data retention and account deletion
Your personal data is retained for as long as necessary to operate your account and deliver your CAPS, subject to applicable legal obligations.
Retention and deletion of CAPS
Accepted CAPS are retained until their opening date, including where it is postponed until the recipient turns 18. Their content is then accessible and downloadable for
15 days
, even if the recipient views it later.
File deletion is scheduled
15 days after the CAPS is declined, the acceptance deadline expires or the viewing period ends
. An additional 7-day technical protection applies after deletion, without users being able to access the files.
Erasure therefore normally occurs within
approximately 22 days after these events
, subject to processing delays or a technical incident. A file still needed for another active CAPS remains stored for that CAPS.
A record of the CAPS may remain in the history: sending date, sender, recipient and status,
without photos or videos
. Database backups follow a separate cycle of 30 days from their creation, followed by 7 days of technical protection.
Account deletion and wishes

In “My Account”, you can choose whether, if your account is deleted or you die, your CAPS already validated and travelling should continue their journey or be deleted. This choice is confirmed when deleting the account. In the event of death, recorded wishes are taken into account after verification.
If you choose to let your CAPS continue their journey, only the data necessary for their delivery and viewing is retained until the applicable deadlines.

Some authentication data, including the email address and telephone number associated with the account, may take up to 180 days to be permanently erased from Firebase systems after deletion is initiated. This period does not apply to the photos and videos in your CAPS.
Privacy and exceptions

Your personal data will never be handed over to your relatives or loved ones, except for CAPS addressed to them, in accordance with your wishes and the service conditions, subject to legal obligations and court decisions.
Some data may be retained separately to meet a legal obligation or handle a dispute. Files downloaded by recipients to their devices cannot be remotely deleted by CAPSOA.
6 - Your rights

You may request access to, correction or deletion of your personal data. Subject to the conditions laid down by regulation, you also have the rights to restriction of processing, objection and data portability.
Where processing is based on your consent, you may withdraw it at any time without affecting processing already lawfully carried out.

To exercise your rights, contact contact@capsoa.fr. These rights also apply to CAPS recipients without an account. In-app editing restrictions do not prevent you from requesting correction of inaccurate information.

You will receive a response within one month. This period may be extended by two months for complex requests or numerous requests; you will be informed of the reasons for the extension within the first month. If there is reasonable doubt about your identity, further information may be requested to verify it.
You may also lodge a complaint with the CNIL at
www.cnil.fr
7 - Hosting and data transfers
Your CAPS’ photos and videos, their backups managed by CAPSOA and the main database are hosted in the European Union.

Some services necessary to operate CAPSOA, including authentication and certain technical processing, nevertheless involve data processing in the United States. The providers listed in Article 3 may also involve teams or subcontractors outside the European Union, particularly in India for support and maintenance.

Depending on the services concerned, these transfers are governed by the mechanisms provided for in the GDPR: adequacy decisions or European Commission standard contractual clauses, supplemented where necessary by additional protection measures.
For details or a copy of the applicable safeguards, contact contact@capsoa.fr.
8 - Changes to the privacy policy
This policy may be updated to reflect changes to CAPSOA, the use of personal data or regulations. The last update date appears at the top of this page.

Any significant change concerning the use of your data will be communicated appropriately in the app or by email. Where your consent is required, it will be requested before the processing concerned is implemented.

TERMS OF USE
Last updated: 24 October 2026
Article 1 — Purpose and scope
These Terms of Use ("CGU") define the conditions for accessing and using the CAPSOA application.

CAPSOA allows digital time capsules, called “Caps”, containing personal content to be created, preserved and sent to one or more recipients. They are scheduled to open on a date and at a time chosen by their creator, according to the features and terms of the selected offer.
These CGU govern use of the application by Caps creators and recipients, as well as access to features available without an account.

The conditions for purchasing paid services are set out in the Terms of Sale (“CGV”). The arrangements for processing personal data are described in the Privacy Policy. Specific provisions for users who are minors are set out in the conditions dedicated to them.
Article 2 — Creating and securing a user account
A user account is required to access CAPSOA features that require identification. Certain features, including the contact form, remain accessible without an account.

Users undertake to provide accurate information when registering, including their date of birth and contact details, and to keep it up to date. They must use an email address and, where a telephone number is requested, a number to which they personally have access. They complete the verifications requested by the application to confirm that they control these contact details.
Users must keep their password and verification codes confidential. They must not disclose them to third parties and must take reasonable precautions to prevent unauthorised access to their account.
If users lose access, suspect hacking or become aware of unauthorised use of their account, they are encouraged to contact CAPSOA promptly and use the recovery or security measures provided.
These duties do not relieve CAPSOA of its own security obligations and do not automatically make users liable for fraudulent use of their account.
Access conditions for users who are minors are set out in the provisions dedicated to them.
Article 3 — Use of the service and content
Users undertake to use CAPSOA lawfully, respectfully towards others and in accordance with these CGU.

Users are responsible for the content they create, import or transmit through the application. They must ensure they hold the rights and permissions needed to use and transmit it, particularly concerning third parties’ privacy, image rights and intellectual property.

CAPSOA must not be used to create, preserve or transmit unlawful content, including threatening, defamatory or fraudulent content, content inciting hatred or violence, or content infringing the rights of others.
It is also prohibited to use the application to harass anyone, impersonate someone, send abusive or repeated messages, circumvent a block or security measures, or disrupt the service.
CAPSOA does not systematically read or review Caps content before transmission. This absence of systematic monitoring does not relieve CAPSOA of its legal obligations.
Users can report content or behaviour that may be unlawful or contrary to these CGU by contacting CAPSOA.

CAPSOA examines reports received and, where a breach is established or immediate protection is necessary, takes necessary and proportionate measures in accordance with applicable regulations. These measures may include restricting access to the content concerned, removing it or suspending the account. CAPSOA also acts on requests from the competent authorities under the conditions laid down by law. The user concerned is informed of the reasons and ways to challenge the decision under the conditions laid down by applicable regulations.
Article 4 — Recipients and acceptance of Caps
The creator of a Caps must ensure that each recipient’s contact details are accurate and that using them to send an invitation through CAPSOA is legitimate.

Recipients are informed of the Caps through the communication channels provided by the service. They have seven days from the sending of the initial invitation to accept or refuse the Caps. Any reminders do not restart this period.
To accept or refuse the Caps, recipients must have a CAPSOA account and complete the necessary checks to confirm that they are the intended recipient of the invitation.

Acceptance enables the Caps to be preserved for opening on the scheduled date, subject to applicable access conditions. It does not entail any payment or subscription for the recipient. Viewing the invitation or closing the decision window without responding constitutes neither acceptance nor refusal.
For a Caps Mystère, the opening date and time remain confidential and are not disclosed to the recipient before opening.

Recipients remain free to refuse the Caps. If neither acceptance nor refusal is received by the deadline, the invitation expires. The consequences of refusal or expiry for the Caps and for the sums paid by its creator are set out in the CGV. Data retention periods and deletion arrangements are described in the Privacy Policy.
CAPSOA does not intervene in personal relationships between creators and recipients. This provision does not limit CAPSOA’s legal obligations or liabilities.
Article 5 — Privacy and personal data

CAPSOA processes the personal data necessary to manage accounts; create, preserve and transmit Caps; inform recipients; handle support requests; ensure service security; and comply with its legal obligations.
This processing concerns, in particular, application users and recipients whose contact details are provided by Caps creators, even where they do not yet have a CAPSOA account.

CAPSOA does not sell users’ or recipients’ personal data. Some processing requires service providers, particularly for hosting, payment and sending communications. The categories of data recipients and their roles are set out in the Privacy Policy.

CAPSOA does not systematically read or review Caps content, in accordance with Article 3. CAPSOA implements appropriate technical and organisational measures to protect data against unauthorised access, loss, alteration or disclosure.

The Privacy Policy sets out, in particular, the controller’s identity, the data processed, the purposes and legal bases of processing, retention periods, data recipients and, where applicable, transfers outside the European Union and associated safeguards.

It also describes data subjects’ rights, the conditions and arrangements for exercising them, and the possibility of lodging a complaint with the CNIL. Information specific to processing minors’ data is provided there or in dedicated supplementary information.

Acceptance of these CGU does not constitute consent to processing requiring specific consent. Where such consent is required, it is obtained separately and may be withdrawn at any time without affecting the lawfulness of processing previously carried out on that basis.
Article 6 — Operation of the service and responsibilities
CAPSOA operates the application and preserves and makes Caps available in accordance with the commitments of the chosen offer, these CGU, the CGV and applicable legal provisions.

Access to the application may be temporarily interrupted, particularly for maintenance, updates or security operations. CAPSOA endeavours to limit the duration and consequences of these interruptions and, where possible, to inform users in advance. These interruptions do not deprive users of their statutory rights.

Users must ensure the accuracy of the information and contact details they provide and comply with the application’s terms of use. The consequences of an error or misuse are assessed according to their cause and the respective responsibilities of the parties, in accordance with applicable regulations.

CAPSOA implements appropriate technical and organisational measures to protect and preserve Caps for the agreed period. In the event of an incident, CAPSOA takes the necessary steps to limit its consequences, restore the service and, where technically possible, restore the data concerned. Affected users are informed under the conditions laid down by applicable regulations.

Using technical service providers does not relieve CAPSOA of its obligations towards users. An outage, technical failure or cyberattack does not automatically constitute force majeure. Force majeure is assessed under the conditions laid down by law.

If CAPSOA breaches its obligations, users retain the remedies and guarantees provided by applicable regulations. No provision of these CGU removes or limits CAPSOA’s liability or a user’s right where this is prohibited by law.
Article 7 — Changes to the CGU
CAPSOA may amend these CGU, particularly to reflect changes in regulations, application features or technical and security needs, while respecting users’ rights.

Each new version includes an update date and, if different, an effective date. Changes affecting users’ rights or obligations are clearly communicated to them a reasonable time before taking effect, on a medium allowing them to keep the information, including by email.
Where a change requires the user’s agreement, it is obtained expressly. Merely publishing a new version of the CGU does not constitute acceptance by the user.

A new version of the CGU does not retroactively change commitments made for Caps already created and paid for, including their price, essential characteristics, retention period and opening date. Any change to these commitments must be based on the express agreement of the user concerned or on a legal provision authorising or requiring it, under the conditions it sets out.

Urgent measures necessary for service security may be implemented without notice where circumstances warrant. They remain proportionate and cannot remove users’ statutory rights. Affected users are informed as soon as possible, unless a legal obligation or security requirement justifies delaying this information.

Where a change to the service legally gives rise to a right to refuse, terminate the contract or obtain a refund, CAPSOA informs affected users of the procedures and deadlines for exercising that right.
8 - Applicable law and dispute resolution:

These Terms of Use are governed by French law. In the event of a difficulty or dispute concerning the use of CAPSOA, users are encouraged to contact CAPSOA first to seek an amicable solution. Users acting as consumers may also, after first making a complaint to CAPSOA that has not resulted in a satisfactory solution, refer the matter free of charge to the consumer mediator responsible for CAPSOA, in accordance with applicable legal provisions. If no amicable solution is reached, the dispute may be brought before the competent courts in accordance with the applicable ordinary rules of law.
9 - Conditions applicable to minors:

Use of CAPSOA involving a minor is subject to specific rules concerning, in particular, the creation, receipt and opening of Caps. These rules are detailed on the “Use of CAPSOA by minors” page, accessible [here]. Users undertake to read these provisions when a Caps involves a minor.
10 - Exceptional circumstances – Death (Force majeure)
Death of the creator: account closure and the future of Caps
If a user dies, their relatives or loved ones may contact CAPSOA using the contact form or at contact@capsoa.fr to report the death and request closure of the account.

Before taking any action, CAPSOA verifies the request. Supporting documents may be requested, including a death certificate and the information needed to verify the requester’s identity and authority to act. Only information necessary for these checks is requested.
After verification, CAPSOA consults the wishes recorded by the user in their account:
If they wished their Caps to reach their recipients

, the Caps concerned continue their journey until the scheduled opening date, under the conditions of the selected offer. Closing the account does not delete these Caps: the content and data needed for their delivery are retained for the specified periods.
If they wished their Caps to be deleted
, CAPSOA deletes them and closes the account, subject to applicable statutory retention obligations.
A request from a relative or loved one does not, in itself, allow the wishes expressed by the user to be changed.
Confidentiality of Caps content

The content of all Caps remains confidential, whether they are retained or deleted. Reporting the death or requesting closure of the account does not give family members, loved ones or any other third party a right to access this content.
Retained Caps may only be viewed by their designated recipients, under the scheduled opening conditions. Deleted Caps are not passed on to loved ones before deletion.
This confidentiality is subject to the legal obligations imposed on CAPSOA.
Death of the recipient

In the event of the recipient’s death, Caps already accepted and locked continue their normal cycle and are delivered on the scheduled date, in accordance with the conditions defined when they were created.
Financial terms
The death of either party does not constitute grounds for cancellation and does not entitle anyone to a refund for Caps already validated and paid for.

These Terms of Sale (“CGV”) define the conditions applicable to orders for services offered by CAPSOA in its application.

They govern, in particular, the creation and purchase of the different categories of Caps, their payment, modification, preservation, transmission to recipients and opening, and any refunds or credits.

They also apply to orders whose amount is reduced to zero by a promotional offer, promotional code or use of a credit, according to the conditions of the offer concerned.

Before confirming an order, users can read these CGV and must accept them. The essential characteristics of the chosen service, its total price and the conditions of its performance are presented clearly and comprehensibly before the order is definitively confirmed.

The general conditions for accessing and using the application are set out in the Terms of Use (“CGU”), which supplement these CGV.

Caps Instant — A surprise in just a few days. This €1.99 offer is available only when sending from a confirmed CAPSOA contact’s profile. It includes one video of up to 1 minute and 100 MB, and up to 10 photos. Opening may only be scheduled between 3 and 8 days after creation. Other offers retain their standard process.

CAPSOA offers several categories of Caps whose characteristics, maximum scheduling period, permitted number of recipients and price vary according to the chosen offer.
The offers available or planned by CAPSOA are:
• Caps Solo: scheduling up to 1 year into the future — 1 recipient.
• Caps Souvenir: scheduling up to 5 years into the future — 1 recipient.
• Caps Mystère: scheduling up to 5 years into the future — 1 recipient. The opening date and time chosen by the creator are not disclosed to the recipient before the Caps opens.
• Caps Héritage: scheduling up to 30 years into the future — up to 10 recipients. Caps Héritage is planned for a later version. It cannot be ordered in the current version. Its final characteristics and price will be specified when it goes on sale.
The type, number, duration and limits of content that may be included in each Caps are specified in the offer description within the application before ordering and form part of the characteristics of the service purchased.
The detailed characteristics and tax-inclusive price of each offer are presented before the user confirms their order.
The SMS surcharge for a second attempt with a telephone number is €0.59, in addition to any Caps price. It is presented before payment and remains separate from the credit, under the conditions of Article 8. The creator may choose email-only delivery to avoid this surcharge.
The applicable price is the one displayed when ordering. Subsequent price changes do not affect Caps already ordered and paid for.
CAPSOA may occasionally offer promotions, promotional codes or benefits. Their terms of use, validity period and any restrictions are specified when the offer is made.

Before confirming an order, users provide the information necessary to create the Caps, including its content, recipient(s), and desired opening date and time, within the limits of the chosen offer.

A summary allows users to check the Caps’ characteristics, the information provided and the total price, and to correct any errors before final confirmation.

Users accept these CGV before confirming their order. Where payment is required, the order is validated after payment confirmation. The ordering function clearly indicates the obligation to pay. Where a promotional offer, code or credit reduces the amount to zero, users confirm their order without a bank payment.

CAPSOA provides order confirmation on a durable medium allowing users to retain it and reproduce it unchanged. This confirmation includes legally required information unless already supplied on such a medium. It is sent within a reasonable time after conclusion of the contract and before performance of the service begins.

From order validation, users have 24 hours to modify their Caps under Article 4. At the end of this period, the Caps is locked and enters the recipient invitation process under Article 5.

This modification period neither replaces nor limits any statutory right of withdrawal, the arrangements for which are set out in Article 9.

Before confirming their order, users tick a box acknowledging that they have been informed of the 24-hour modification period and the financial consequences of voluntary deletion. Creators may delete their Caps during this period and during its journey after locking. Such deletion does not, in itself, entitle them to a refund or credit, subject to statutory rights and the refund conditions applicable to the App Store or Google Play. The arrangements are set out in Article 8.

From order validation, creators have 24 hours to modify their Caps’ content and the information that the application allows them to change.

During this period, the application identifies the Caps as editable. Creators are responsible for checking its content and the information provided before the period ends.

After 24 hours, the Caps is automatically locked: its creator can no longer change its content. The recipient invitation process then begins under Article 5. Preserving the Caps until opening is subject to acceptance by the recipient under these CGV.

Locking does not prevent creators from voluntarily deleting their Caps during its journey. This is also possible during the 24-hour modification period.

Voluntary deletion of a Caps does not, in itself, entitle the user to a refund or credit, subject to their statutory rights and the refund conditions applicable to the App Store or Google Play, in accordance with Article 8.

The 24-hour modification period is separate from any statutory right of withdrawal, addressed in Article 9.
5 - Informing recipients and the seven-day response period:

Caps Instant exception: after the 24-hour editing period, the recipient receives the invitation and has 48 hours to accept or decline, regardless of the chosen opening date. The seven-day period described below does not apply to this offer. If accepted in time, the Caps stays closed until the scheduled opening time. Without a response within these 48 hours, it is archived and a credit is granted under Article 8.

After the 24-hour modification period, the Caps is locked and CAPSOA sends an invitation to the recipient designated by the creator through the communication channels provided by the service.

Each recipient has seven days from the sending of the initial invitation to accept or refuse the Caps. If necessary, they must create an account and complete the required verifications before communicating their decision.

CAPSOA may send reminders during this period. Reminders neither extend nor restart the response period.

Viewing the invitation or Caps presentation constitutes neither acceptance nor refusal. Recipients must express their choice using the actions provided in the application.

If accepted, the Caps continues its journey and is preserved to be made available at the scheduled date and time under these CGV. Recipients do not have to pay to accept or view the Caps.

If explicitly refused, the Caps does not continue its journey to that recipient, and the creator is informed. A recipient’s refusal does not constitute grounds for a refund or credit. The general provisions of Article 8 remain applicable.

If no response is received within seven days, the Caps is considered unsuccessful for that recipient. The creator is informed and receives a credit under Article 8.

Repeated sends to the same recipient are subject to the limit of two unanswered attempts and the reset conditions in Article 8, regardless of how the recipient is identified.

Once accepted by the recipient, CAPSOA preserves the Caps until the opening date and time scheduled by its creator, under these CGV and unless voluntarily deleted by the creator.

During this period, the Caps is considered “on its journey” and its content remains inaccessible to the recipient.

At the scheduled date and time, CAPSOA automatically makes the content accessible and may inform the recipient through the service’s notifications.

For a Caps Mystère, the opening date and time remain hidden from the recipient until that point.

During the Caps’ journey, the creator’s identity may be presented under a nickname or anonymously. When the Caps opens, the creator’s real surname and first name are revealed to the recipient.

Recipients have 15 days from the scheduled opening date and time to view and download the content. Viewing it late does not extend this period. Recipients are responsible for saving any content they wish to keep during this period.

After these 15 days, the content is no longer accessible and is automatically deleted. The Caps is archived in the history: this archive retains a record of its existence and journey, without providing access to deleted content.

Users must keep their contact details up to date and retain access to their account to receive notifications and view their Caps.

The total Caps price is presented in euros, including all taxes where applicable, before order confirmation.

Paid purchases use the App Store or Google Play in-app purchase system, depending on the platform used. Available payment methods and payment authorisation arrangements are those offered by that platform.

CAPSOA neither collects nor retains the full bank card details used for these purchases.

An order for a paid Caps is validated only after payment confirmation and purchase verification. Until confirmation is obtained, including where payment is pending, declined or cancelled, the Caps does not enter the recipient invitation process.

If payment appears completed on the platform but the Caps is not recorded in the application, users may contact CAPSOA support with the purchase reference so that it can be checked.

Where a promotional offer, code or credit reduces the order amount to zero, no payment is required. The order is then validated through the application’s designated flow.

Use of a promotional code or credit is subject to the validity conditions and restrictions communicated before use.

Conditions relating to credits and refunds are set out in Article 8.

Caps Instant exception: if there is no response within 48 hours of the invitation, after the 24-hour editing period, the creator receives a credit usable for a Caps Instant or a Caps Solo. For this credit, these rules replace the same-offer restriction and the seven-day period stated below. If a Caps funded by this credit also receives no response, the renewed credit remains usable for Instant or Solo; it is granted according to the response period of the selected offer. All other credit conditions continue to apply.

Unless otherwise required by law or expressly provided in these CGV, sums paid to create a Caps are non-refundable.

Voluntary deletion by the creator and explicit refusal by the recipient give rise to neither a refund nor a credit. Acceptance followed by availability on the scheduled date likewise does not entitle the creator to a refund simply for changing their mind. The preservation and viewing obligations in Article 6 remain applicable.

If a recipient does not respond within seven days of the initial invitation being sent, the creator receives a credit to create a new Caps of the same plan. This credit is personal, single-use and valid for one month from its date of issue. Its expiry date is shown in your “My promo codes” section. It is not money that can be withdrawn or transferred and does not cover any SMS surcharges.

If a Caps created using this credit also remains unanswered after the same period, a new credit for the same plan is issued. There is no overall maximum number of renewals, subject to the contact limits below and the validity of the initial funding. A refunded or cancelled initial purchase cannot form the basis for new credits.

To limit repeated contact, a creator cannot send more than two unanswered Caps to the same recipient. This rule applies to CAPSOA contacts and people without an account, whether identified by email, telephone number or both. A third send is blocked; the credit remains usable for another recipient. Two Caps already awaiting a response also prevent a new send until their status is resolved. Verified contact details and identities linked to the same account are considered together.

The counter resets when that recipient actually sends a Caps back to the creator. Two further attempts are then possible. To preserve anonymity, if the return Caps sender’s identity is hidden, the reset occurs when that identity is revealed at opening.

On the first attempt, the SMS provided in the invitation flow is included. After an unanswered first attempt, retaining a telephone number for a second attempt incurs a €0.59 SMS surcharge, even when an email address is also provided and even if the Caps is created using a credit. An alert lets the creator choose: remove the number and use email only, without an SMS surcharge, or retain the number and accept the surcharge before payment. Reminder emails and the SMS are sent according to the invitation flow and applicable reminder rules. Sending is not systematic once the recipient has responded.

The commercial credits described above do not replace a refund required by law. Consumers’ statutory rights, including in the event of failure to supply or lack of conformity of the service, and the conditions applicable to refund requests through the App Store or Google Play remain applicable.

Independently of these rights, users may contact CAPSOA support to request review of an exceptional situation. CAPSOA may offer an appropriate commercial solution, without review of the request guaranteeing acceptance.
9 - Right of withdrawal and refund conditions:

A consumer has fourteen days from conclusion of the contract to exercise their right of withdrawal without having to justify the decision, subject to statutory exceptions and extensions.

The twenty-four-hour modification period in Article 4 allows changes to Caps content. It is distinct from the statutory withdrawal period. Its expiry and the locking of the Caps do not, on their own, constitute a waiver of the right of withdrawal.

Where users expressly request that performance begin before the withdrawal period expires, CAPSOA obtains that request and provides legally required information. If they withdraw after the service has begun, users remain liable for an amount proportionate to services actually provided up to communication of their decision, where the conditions of Article L221-25 of the French Consumer Code are met. This amount must be justified; no flat-rate withdrawal penalty applies. No amount is due on this basis where the legal requirements for obtaining the express request or providing information have not been met.

The right of withdrawal can no longer be exercised where the service has been fully performed before the fourteen days expire, provided performance began with the user’s prior express agreement and the user acknowledged that this right would be lost once the service was fully performed. Acceptance of these CGV alone does not replace those consents.

Once a Caps accepted by its recipient has reached its scheduled opening date and time, making it available does not give rise to a commercial refund simply because the creator changes their mind. This rule does not prevent exercise of a statutory right of withdrawal that still applies or other statutory consumer rights. Making a Caps available or opening it does not, on its own, prove complete performance of all CAPSOA’s obligations.

To exercise this right, users communicate their decision to CAPSOA before the applicable deadline, using the standard withdrawal form or any unambiguous statement, including through “Contact CAPSOA”. They are encouraged to provide their order reference and identifying information. Absence of a reference does not deprive users of their right where the order can otherwise be identified.

CAPSOA may check the information needed to process the request, including the transaction, consents obtained, services actually provided and refunds already made. These checks cannot make exercise of the right of withdrawal subject to prior authorisation or extend the statutory refund period. An amount already refunded does not entitle the user to a second refund of that amount.

Where withdrawal entitles the user to a refund, CAPSOA returns the sums due without undue delay and no later than fourteen days after communication of the decision, deducting only the amount that may lawfully remain due for services already provided. The same payment method is used unless the user expressly agrees to another method that entails no fees. A credit cannot be imposed instead of a legally owed refund.

For App Store or Google Play purchases, users may also use the relevant store’s refund procedure. Those stores’ processing arrangements do not limit applicable statutory rights.

Outside a statutory right to a refund, requests for a goodwill gesture fall under Article 8. Reviewing them neither acknowledges a refund obligation nor commits to granting a credit.

CAPSOA implements the technical and organisational resources necessary for the proper operation, security and availability of the service, and for preserving and making Caps available under the conditions agreed when ordering.

Access to the application may be temporarily interrupted or disrupted, particularly for maintenance, updates, technical incidents or necessary security measures. CAPSOA endeavours to limit the duration and consequences of these interruptions and, where possible, to notify users in advance of planned operations.

Where an incident affects a Caps’ preservation or accessibility on the scheduled date, CAPSOA takes appropriate steps to identify its cause, limit its consequences and restore the service without undue delay. Where data is affected, CAPSOA undertakes technically possible restoration operations and informs affected users of the identified consequences.

A temporary interruption does not, on its own, trigger an automatic refund where contractual commitments remain fulfilled. However, where an incident constitutes failure to supply or lack of conformity of the service, users benefit from statutory remedies, which may include restoring the service, a price reduction or termination with a refund, under the applicable conditions.

In the event of permanent loss of a Caps or permanent inability to perform the purchased service, CAPSOA informs the creator and refunds the sums legally due. A credit or replacement may be offered but cannot be imposed instead of a refund to which the user is entitled.

Users may report incidents through the “Contact CAPSOA” form, providing information useful to identify the Caps and the problem. There is no need to provide the Caps’ private content to make this report.

This article does not limit applicable statutory guarantees or users’ right to compensation for damage under the conditions laid down by law.

If the service closes permanently, CAPSOA informs affected users as soon as possible and explains the consequences for their Caps and the proposed steps.

Where technically possible, CAPSOA allows creators to recover their content before closure. The arrangements and recovery deadline are communicated to them. No early opening for a recipient takes place without the creator’s agreement or by circumventing restrictions applicable to minors.

Where closure prevents performance of a purchased service, users’ statutory rights remain applicable, including concerning refunds of sums due. Recovering content does not remove these rights.

After the announced recovery period, content is deleted according to the arrangements communicated, subject to statutory retention obligations.
12 - Complaints, mediation, applicable law and dispute resolution:

In the event of a difficulty or complaint concerning an order or the service, users may contact CAPSOA using the “Contact CAPSOA” form, providing information useful to identify their request. CAPSOA examines complaints and responds within a reasonable time.

If a prior written complaint to CAPSOA has not resolved the dispute, consumers may refer the matter free of charge to the consumer mediator responsible for CAPSOA, subject to statutory admissibility conditions. The mediation request must be submitted within one year of the written complaint to CAPSOA.

In accordance with the provisions of the French Consumer Code concerning the consumer dispute mediation process, after contacting us and if you have not received a satisfactory response, you may use a consumer mediation procedure free of charge through:

CM2C
49 rue de Ponthieu
75 008 PARIS
Tel. : 01 89 47 00 14
Website :

Mediation is optional for consumers. Both parties remain free to accept or refuse the mediator’s proposed solution.

These CGV are governed by French law. This choice does not deprive consumers of mandatory protections under the law applicable to their situation, including the law of their country of habitual residence where the statutory conditions are met.

Any dispute may be brought before the competent courts under the applicable rules. No provision of these CGV imposes exclusive jurisdiction of the courts where CAPSOA is established on consumers or limits their access to justice.
